state.row_3_19_done_when: Masks (add, subtract, intersect, difference; feather; expansion), clip groups, alpha and luma mattes and trim start/end/offset render on the GPU and match CPU references; the scene contract's trim values are honoured (they are silently ignored today); an unsupported combination refuses by name.
user_decisions_15_nov: A track matte names its source by explicit id: ObjectBase.trackMatte {sourceId, mode}, modes alpha, alphaInverted, luma, lumaInverted (After Effects 2023 and later, where any layer can be the matte and several layers can share one).
Mattes composite per frame: the compositor renders the matte source into its own tile target each frame and the consumer layer's sample is multiplied by the matte there.

Clip groups (done): a clip child is composited per frame into a matte target at its own opacity (not its effective opacity, which would apply a group's opacity twice), whether visible or not, and is never drawn itself; nested clips multiply.
facts: Every drawing object is drawn once at prepare into its own layer texture; per frame the GPU warps and blends it. Groups paint nothing; effective transform, opacity and visibility multiply down from ancestors.
Colour is composited premultiplied in the project working space (sRGB-encoded or linear sRGB); the Rec.709 luma weights are 0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722.

In After Effects, choosing a layer as a track matte turns that layer's video switch off, and the matte still works; the user may switch the video back on to see the layer as well. GrapiX objects have one visible flag and no separate video switch.
The matte-target machinery from clip groups already composites a matte layer each frame (its own opacity, its own clip if it sits in a clip group) and multiplies a consumer by the target's alpha.

source_drawn.instructions: Is a track matte source also drawn itself?

criteria.never_drawn: Never: being named as a track matte source makes it a matte only, as a clip child is (After Effects turns its video off when it becomes a matte), whatever its visible flag.
criteria.drawn_when_visible: Drawn when its visible flag is set, and a matte either way, as After Effects allows by switching the video back on.

source_opacity.instructions: Which opacity does the matte source's matte carry?

criteria.own_opacity: Its own opacity, as clip children do: a group's opacity already reaches the consumers in that group.
criteria.effective_opacity: Its effective opacity (own times ancestors'), so fading the source's group fades the matte.

luma.instructions: How is a luma matte value computed?

criteria.rec709_premultiplied: Rec.709 weights over the matte target's premultiplied working-space colour (transparent counts as black), clamped to 0..1; inverted luma is one minus that.
criteria.rec709_straight_times_alpha: Rec.709 weights over the straight (unpremultiplied) colour, then multiplied by alpha.
criteria.linear_always: Convert to linear light first whatever the working space, then Rec.709 weights.

refusals.instructions: Which track mattes should refuse by name (Refusal::TrackMatteInvalid)?

criteria.strict_set: An object naming itself; a source not in the scene; a source or consumer that draws no pixels (group, layer, camera, light, marker, mesh, paint); a source that has a track matte of its own; a clip child that has a track matte. Everything else, including a source inside a clip group, a consumer inside a clip group and several consumers sharing a source, renders.
criteria.permissive: Only a missing source or an object naming itself refuses; chains of mattes and mattes on groups render too.

needs_user.instructions: Must the user approve these before implementation?

criteria.true: Yes, a recorded user decision would change or a new product choice is being made.
criteria.false: No, these follow from the recorded decisions.
